title: Why Bigger Context Windows Won't Save Your Agent — Elizabeth Fuentes Leone, AWS
talk_summary: The talk argues bigger context windows degrade due to attention limits and context poisoning, so agents should externalize, select, compress, and isolate context. It demos Strands conversation managers, memory pointers for large tool outputs, shared invocation-state pointers across agents, max tool-call limits, and async MCP handles to avoid loops and blocking.

takeaways.technique: Externalize large tool outputs as memory pointers
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of putting logs or large data in the context window, a tool saves the data to storage and returns an ID; the agent retrieves it only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: save that logs in a storage and you are going to retrieve an ID

takeaways.technique: Summarize older messages while preserving recent ones
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a conversation manager to summarize older history and keep the last N messages verbatim, optionally summarizing a fixed percentage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep the four last messages and it's going to summarize the other 50%

takeaways.technique: Share invocation-state pointers, not full context
takeaways.what_they_do: In multi-agent swarms, avoid sharing the entire context window; share an ID or memory pointer in invocation state so each agent fetches only what it needs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you share the context window between agents is like add garbage to the other agents

takeaways.what_they_do: Set per-tool maximum invocation counts and clear tool responses so agents cannot loop forever on the same tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you set max tool counts for this example is my tools search fly
takeaways.numbers: example: each tool limited to 3 invocations

takeaways.technique: Async job handles for slow external tools
takeaways.what_they_do: For MCP or external APIs that may not answer promptly, start an async job and retrieve the result later instead of blocking synchronously.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have an a sync handle, you can invoke your NCP, your external API

takeaways.technique: Select relevant context, avoid context stuffing
takeaways.what_they_do: Retrieve only information relevant to the task and avoid passing everything, because irrelevant context can distract or poison the model.
